children.text: A business and commercial district of about 27 hectares built on the site of the old Lahug Airport. It makes a good half-day to full-day outing: shop and eat at Ayala Malls Central Bloc by day, then enjoy the Sugbo Mercado night market and a rooftop bar in the evening. The night market moved to a new spot inside the district in 2026.

Cebu IT Park is a business and commercial district of about 27 hectares in the Apas area in the north of Cebu City, a neighborhood most people simply call Lahug, set just in from Salinas Drive. It is run by Cebu Holdings, part of the Ayala Land group, and used to be called Asiatown IT Park. Call centers and IT service centers of multinationals such as Accenture, IBM and JPMorgan Chase fill one office building after another, with a shopping mall, hotels, condominiums and a night market tucked in between. Because so many people here work through the night on US and European hours, restaurants, cafes and convenience stores stay lit and people are out on the streets even at midnight, and that is the district's most distinctive trait.
This land was originally an airport. Lahug Airport opened as a military airfield in
June 1938
, became a national airport on
August 12, 1947
and served as Cebu's gateway until operations stopped on
April 27, 1966
, when the airport function moved to Mactan Island. On
February 19, 1981

Pope John Paul II celebrated an open-air Mass on the old runway before a crowd of one million. It was the first papal Mass ever held in Cebu. Later the Philippine Economic Zone Authority (PEZA) approved the site as an economic zone on
April 6, 2000
, and after a presidential proclamation made it an IT special economic zone on
February 27, 2001
, today's forest of buildings began to grow where the runway had been.
The district is small enough to cross on foot from end to end in
10–15 minutes
. Its center is V. Padriga Street, home to the Seda hotel and Ayala Malls Central Bloc, which opened on
December 6, 2019

, and beside it lies Garden Bloc, a green space of about 3 hectares with big trees and a lawn. Over by Geonzon Street is the transport terminal, where jeepneys, the airport bus and the Tops Lookout shuttle stop.
brought big changes. The Cebu BRT (bus rapid transit) began partial operations on
March 13
, making IT Park its northern terminus, and Sugbo Mercado, the night market that had stood in Garden Bloc since
, left that site at the end of
June
and moved to an open lot beside the JPMorgan Chase building. Older guides and map pins often still point to the former location.
Where the
Cebu City

entry covers the daytime old town of Magellan's Cross and the Basilica del Santo Niño, IT Park is the place to see Cebu in the evening and at night. It is not somewhere to come expecting heritage sites or natural scenery. The way to enjoy this neighborhood is to cool off in the air-conditioned mall, then, once the sun goes down, buy grilled skewers and lechon at the night market and have a drink at a rooftop bar. It suits travelers staying at a Mactan resort who want one evening of city atmosphere, families who need an indoor plan on a rainy day, and people in Cebu for language study or business. The shuttle to
Tops Lookout
on the Busay hills leaves from the district's terminal, so it is also a handy starting point for a night-view outing.
Cebu's best-known food market, which started in Garden Bloc in
with around 25 stalls. "Sugbo" is the Cebuano name for Cebu and "mercado" means market. Since
August 2026
it has been at its new site beside the JPMorgan Chase building, near the 38 Park Avenue condominium, open Tuesday to Sunday from
4 p.m. to midnight
. Entry is free, and you pick from lechon belly, grilled skewers, grilled seafood and Korean- and Japanese-style stall food, then eat at long shared tables.
A five-level mall that opened on
December 6, 2019

, with about 45,000㎡ of leasable space. It has four cinemas, a basement supermarket and a food court, with a hotel rising above it. There is an indoor climbing gym on the second floor, and a trampoline park and a roller-skating rink are also listed as operating, so it is a good place to spend time with children. Opening hours are listed as
Sunday to Thursday and
on Fridays and Saturdays, and they change on public holidays.

A green space of about 3 hectares left open between the buildings, with a lawn and paths under big, wide-spreading trees. The triangular building in the middle, The Pyramid, was used as a restaurant and bar but has been closed since late
, though the structure remains as a photo backdrop. It is nicer to walk here around sunset than at midday.
Since
June 2024
, a rectangular loop of about
1km
of the district's streets has been closed to vehicles every Sunday from
5 to 10 a.m.
The circuit takes in Geonzon Street, Inez Villa Street and others, and local office workers and families come to run and walk. The shade thins out after 8 a.m., so head out early.

blocks.title: Rooftop bar and streets after dark

children.text: The Seda hotel above Central Bloc has a roof deck bar looking down on the lights of the district, and cocktail bars, live-music pubs and karaoke venues are scattered in and around it. With so many shift workers, there are customers even on weeknights. Drinks at bars in Cebu City run about
for a beer and about
for a cocktail, depending on the venue and the season.
The runway is gone but the story remains. The Chapel of St. John Paul II on the fourth floor of Central Bloc is named after the pope who celebrated Mass on this spot in
, and shoppers and office workers gather there together for weekend Masses. It is a quiet prayer space in the middle of a mall, so be respectful when you drop in.
A shuttle to
Tops Lookout
on the Busay hills leaves from the IT Park transport terminal on Geonzon Street. It costs
including the round trip and the entrance fee, and takes about
20 minutes
each way. A good order is to go up an hour before sunset, take in the night view, then come down for dinner at the night market.

blocks.title: Resting or working in a cafe

children.text: Chain coffee shops and independent cafes are all over the district, and people working on laptops are a common sight. Property consultancy Colliers counted about 10,500 seats here, 75% of Metro Cebu's flexible workspace seats. Several coworking operators have set up in the district, which makes it convenient for travelers combining work and travel.
Take a Grab or taxi to Ayala Malls Central Bloc, look around the mall and cool off in a cafe
Walk along V. Padriga Street and through Garden Bloc, photographing The Pyramid and the forest of buildings
Head to Sugbo Mercado beside the JPMorgan Chase building. Grab a table before it gets busy and go around the stalls for dinner
Return to the mall for dessert, or buy gifts such as dried mangoes at the supermarket
Have a drink with the night view at the Seda hotel's roof deck bar or a bar nearby
Book a Grab back to where you are staying

On a rainy day, have dinner in the mall's dining area instead of the night market and switch to the cinema and other indoor facilities. For the old-town heritage sites, it is less hot to combine them with the itinerary in the
Cebu City
entry in the morning and come over here late in the afternoon.

items.title: From Manila and Korea to Cebu

children.text: From Manila it is about
1 hour 20 minutes
by air to Mactan-Cebu International Airport (CEB), with Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific flying dozens of flights a day. From Incheon, nonstop flights take about
4 hours 30 minutes
The airport is on Mactan Island, and IT Park is about
15km
away across a bridge. Airport terminals and airlines are covered in detail in the
Cebu City
entry.

items.title: Taxi or Grab from the airport

children.text: It takes
30–45 minutes
in lighter traffic and up to
1 hour–1 hour 15 minutes
at rush hour. Congestion is worst on the bridges linking Mactan and mainland Cebu.
Grab fares vary widely from one guide to another, so allow about
, and about
for a yellow airport taxi. Base fares for app-hailed cars rose 20% from
September 28, 2026
, so check the amount in the app before you ride.
Enter a specific destination such as "Ayala Malls Central Bloc" or your hotel's name rather than "Cebu IT Park," or you may be dropped at the wrong entrance.
Since
March 14, 2025
, a MyBus route has linked the airport directly with the IT Park transport terminal. The fare is
and it runs via Parkmall and SM City Cebu.
Buses from the airport to IT Park are listed as running
and those from IT Park to the airport
, leaving about once an hour. The timetable changes often, and you will wait longer at busy times.
The Cebu BRT, which began partial operations on
March 13, 2026
, runs from Il Corso in the SRP via the South Bus Terminal, Fuente Osmeña and the Capitol to IT Park. The fare is
for the first
5km
and rises with distance after that.

In its early months only 17 of the 30 buses were running, and some sections share ordinary traffic lanes, so it is slow at rush hour. Free-ride hours and stops may change, so check the latest announcements.
The 17B jeepney runs from Apas and IT Park through Lahug, the Capitol, Fuente Osmeña and Colon Street to Carbon Market. For Ayala Center Cebu and SM City Cebu, board the 04L near JY Square.
From
September 28, 2026
the minimum fare is
on traditional jeepneys and
on modern jeepneys. Route numbers are painted on the windshield and the sides, so confirm the destination with the driver before boarding.

items.title: Taxi or Grab from within the city

children.text: From Ayala Center Cebu it is
10–15 minutes
by car (when there is no congestion), and from the old town the fare comes to about
. From 5 to 8 p.m. the roads into the district are badly congested.
To go straight to Sugbo Mercado, enter "Cebu IT Park, Inez Villa Street" as the destination and you will be dropped close to the new site.
Inside the district the sidewalks and crossings are well kept, and there is lighting and security at night, so walking is easy. From the mall, the night market and the transport terminal are all
5–10 minutes
away on foot.
The main roads outside the district carry heavy traffic, so when heading out at night it is better to take a Grab even for a short distance.
In Cebu the dry season runs
December–May
, with the least rain in
February–April
. Average highs are about
in January and about

in May, the hottest month, so it is hot all year. Because IT Park's attractions are concentrated in the mall and the evening night market, the season matters little, but the night market is outdoors with only tents for a roof, so a clear evening is best. A comfortable plan is to stay indoors at midday and head outside from around
5 p.m.
In the
June–November

rainy season, showers are frequent in the afternoon and evening, and monthly rainfall tops 200mm in July and October. In a downpour the night market empties out and Grabs become hard to get. Cebu is less affected by typhoons than the eastern Philippines, but this district and its mall were damaged by Typhoon Odette in
December 2021
, and much of Metro Cebu was flooded by Typhoon Tino on
November 4, 2025
. Around the Sinulog Festival on the third Sunday of
January
, hotel prices jump and rooms fill early, so book ahead.

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
The most convenient place to stay in the district is Seda Central Bloc Cebu, which sits on top of the Central Bloc mall. Opened in

, it is a 17-story business hotel with 214 rooms, a swimming pool and a roof deck bar, and being directly above the mall makes it easy to come and go even on rainy days. Across Salinas Drive, the Waterfront Cebu City Hotel & Casino is a large, long-established hotel within walking distance of the district. Four-star hotels cost about
a night depending on the date, and mid-range hotels around Lahug run roughly
. To save on lodging, you can also stay at a budget hotel near Ayala Center Cebu or SM City Cebu and come over only in the evening.

Sugbo Mercado is the heart of the food scene. Crisp-skinned lechon belly, charcoal-grilled pork and chicken skewers, grilled squid and shrimp, and upright-roasted whole chicken are the favorites, mixed in with foreign-food stalls selling takoyaki, ramen, samgyeopsal and shawarma. For dessert there are halo-halo and fruit shakes. Pork skewers cost about
, grilled seafood about
and a rice meal about
. Most stalls take cash only and just a few accept GCash, and the rule is that diners clear their own dishes when they finish. On some nights there are live performances on a small stage.

On days when the night market is closed or it is raining, Central Bloc is the alternative. A dining zone called Food Choices and the food court bring together Filipino food, Korean barbecue, Japanese food and fast food, and you can buy fruit and snacks at the basement supermarket. The district has convenience stores and fast-food outlets open late into the night, so you can find a meal even at a late hour. Shops change often, so for any place you really want to visit, check on a map app that it is open before you go. Cebu's famous lechon specialists and the Larsian barbecue alley are covered in the
Cebu City
entry.
The tables at Sugbo Mercado are full from around
7 p.m.
Go at
and secure a table first, then have one person hold it while the others buy the food.
The night market is known to open Tuesday to Sunday, but some listings say it opens on Mondays too. If you plan to go on a Monday, check that week's notice on Sugbo Mercado's Facebook page.
Small bills of ₱20, ₱50 and ₱100 are handiest at the stalls. If you run short of cash, use an ATM inside the district.
The way to enjoy the night market is to go as a group, order a little from three or four stalls and share. Lechon tastes best early in the evening, when it is freshly carved.
The air conditioning in the mall and cinemas is strong, so bring a light layer. Bags are checked at the mall entrances.
On Friday and Saturday evenings the parking lots in the district fill up before
Even if you have rented a car, a Grab is easier on those days.
Grab bookings take a long time at the evening rush hour. On days when you need to get to the airport or the port, allow twice the usual time.
Bars and clubs check IDs, and some will not admit people in flip-flops or sleeveless tops (many do not enforce this strictly, but avoid beachwear). In the Philippines you must be 18 to buy alcohol.
The Tops shuttle runs until late at night, but the time of the last trip differs from guide to guide. On the way up, ask the driver when the last shuttle down leaves.
Sugbo Mercado left its old site (Garden Bloc), in front of Avida Towers and beside the transport terminal, at the end of
June 2026

. It now operates beside the JPMorgan Chase building, on the Inez Villa Street side. Older blogs and some maps still point to the former site, so check the location and opening days on the official Facebook page before you go.
The district itself is relatively safe, but pickpockets operate in the crowded night market and on jeepneys. Wear your bag in front and do not leave your phone on the table.
After drinking, do not walk out of the district; book a Grab instead. Politely decline drinks offered by strangers.
Shops change often. The Pyramid has been closed since late
and The Park Social closed on
February 20, 2024
. Restaurants and bars mentioned in older articles may no longer exist.
In
August 2025
Ayala Malls announced that it would renovate three Cebu malls, including Central Bloc, over three years. Some areas may be blocked off for construction and some shops may be closed.
During rainy-season downpours and typhoons, the surrounding roads flood and you cannot get a ride. If a warning is issued, drop your outdoor plans and stay in your hotel or inside the mall.
In its
July 2026

adjustment of travel advisories, Korea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs kept the Zamboanga Peninsula and the Sulu, Basilan and Tawi-Tawi island groups on its travel ban list, and Cebu is not among them. Still, check your own government's current travel advisory before you leave.
